question_text: In this verse, is the characteristic taken up by a person from another, and if so how does it operate in that uptake? Record none if it is not.

distinct_answers.text: Yes — the receiving of hatred is documented across many verses. Gen 29:31: "Leah was hated" — the condition of being hated named as a state she inhabits. Gen 37:4: Joseph receives his brothers' hatred. Psa 69:4: "those who hate me without cause." Isa 66:5: "your brothers who hate you and cast you out for my name's sake." The receiving of hatred is experienced as a relational condition — not just a series of hostile acts but a state the person is placed in.

Yes. Buz (group 316-001): the sufferer, the poor, and the righteous receive contempt from the comfortable and proud (Job 12:5, Psa 123:3-4). Shut (group 1277-001): Israel receives the contempt of surrounding nations (Eze 28:24). The one who receives contempt is placed outside the circle of the contemner's regard.

Yes — Job 19:19, 30:10, Isa 49:7: being the object of abhorrence from intimate friends and from the nation. Being the recipient of abhorrence places the person outside the circle of the abhorrer's presence entirely.
Yes — the dominant register of group 1775-002 (13 verses). Job 6:23, Isa 25:4, Jer 15:21: the recipient of ruthless domination cries for deliverance and finds shelter in God.

Receiving is the entire structure of M06-E. All 81 verses document the experience of being the recipient of reproach: individual (Psa 69:20), communal (Psa 79:4), unjust (Psa 69:4: "without cause"), just (Jer 31:19: "disgrace of my youth"), voluntary (Jer 15:15: "for your sake I bear reproach"), and involuntary (Psa 22:6).
Yes — the person receives the adversary relationship when another party positions themselves in opposition. Luk 18:3's widow and 1Pe 5:8's believer both receive an adversary's opposition.

The verse evidence does not document the inner experience of those who are the objects of malice. Israel is the implicit recipient but the inner experience of being maliced is not described in the three Ezekiel verses.

The receiving direction is evidenced across all sub-groups but is unevenly documented. M05-A (love received), M05-B (compassion received — the cry for divine compassion), M05-C (mercy cry — Group 1629 — is the most vivid and extensive receiving evidencing in M05), M05-F (comfort received — extensively evidenced in both OT grief contexts and NT apostolic contexts) are the most receiver-prominent sub-groups. M05-D and M05-E are the most giver-oriented in their verse evidence — the receiver's immediate inner experience is underspecified. M05-G documents receiving reconciliation (Rom 5:11 — Group 2069) and being called into fellowship (1Cor 1:9 — Group 1055) as the primary receiving events.

**Conditions enabling reception** are consistent across sub-groups: humility, need, seeking, honest mourning, walking in the light — the posture of the person who acknowledges their need and opens themselves to receive.

**Non-receiving inner states** are also consistent: hardness (M05-A, D), refusal (M05-F), self-deception (M05-G), mercilessness (M05-C), disordered love priority (M05-A).

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — indirectly: the person who receives instruction in righteousness is receiving from another. "I have taught you the way of wisdom; I have led you in the paths of uprightness" (Pro 4:11, VSG 1211-002). The righteousness that comes through teaching and formation is received from the teacher/parent/community.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — justification is received: "being justified by his grace" (Tit 3:7) is a reception event. The mode of reception is through faith — the person receives what God has declared through the act of believing.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — the wronged person receives justice from God through the mediating act of the commissioned human avenger (Rom 13:4) or through God's direct response to the cry (Luk 18:7–8). The reception of justice is the resolution of the wronged person's situation.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — the person receives the verdict of condemnation (external, from judge), the relief of freedom from condemnation (from God through Christ), or the self-condemnation of the conscience (from within, through autokatakritos). All three forms of condemnation-verdict are received.

**[CLUSTER — T4.4]** E. Reception of righteousness from others operates through teaching/formation (A2, B: instruction in right paths), through the declared verdict of justification received by faith (C), through received justice from God or commissioned agents (D), and through received verdict of condemnation or freedom (E). The cluster reveals that righteousness in all its modes is ultimately received — even the human righteousness of A2 is first received through formation and ultimately through God's credit.
VCG03 (Pro 1:5 — "let the wise hear and increase in learning"): wisdom received from human wisdom-bearers.
VCG07 (M15-B — dialegō): understanding received through sustained discourse from a teacher/apostle.
VCG04 (Hos 6:3): communal "let us" — receiving as community. VCG06: the learner receiving from the wise.
VCG05 (ta.am): receiving in M15-D is testing-what-is-received — active evaluation of what comes in.
VCG04 (2Sa 16:23): the king receives counsel. VCG02 (gnōmē, 1Cor 7:25): the community receiving Paul's considered judgment.
VCG02 (Matt 1:20 enthumeomai): the meditative-reflective state opens the person to receive divine and human guidance. The receptive inner state is the condition in which disclosure arrives.
Human-to-human transmission of thought-content not evidenced in M15-G's VCG corpus.
VCG01 (Col 3:16 "richly"): the community receiving the word of Christ mutually.
Receiving from human sources absent from BOUNDARY's evidence.

Yes — strongly. athumeō (Col 3:21): children receive discouragement from parental provocation. ka.eh (Eze 13:22): the righteous receive false disheartening from false prophets. Psa 109:16: the brokenhearted receive cruelty from the wicked. M20-C is the sub-group most clearly showing the characteristic received from another person.

Yes — extensively: Gen 6:8 (889-001 — Noah finding favour); Gen 33:10 (795-003 — Jacob received by Esau); Rut 2:2 (889-002 — Ruth finding favour); 1Sa 2:26 (542-001 — Samuel growing in favour); Luk 1:30 (888-003 — Mary finding favour); Act 7:10 (888-003 — Joseph receiving favour before Pharaoh). The receiving of grace/favour from another person is a pattern across both Testaments and across multiple terms.

Yes — in the receiving-evaluation form: 1Ki 8:18 (God's affirmation received by David — implicitly); 2Sa 3:36 (goodness of the king's action received by the people as approval). The community receiving and affirming goodness is the human-interface form.

M46-C evidences the right reception of material goods: Ecc 5:19 (God gives wealth and the power to enjoy it — the combination of gift and capacity to receive is named). 1Ti 6:17 (God richly provides all things for enjoyment — the enjoyment is the reception of the gift). M46-D shows reception of the kingdom through poverty of spirit (Mat 5:3 — theirs is the kingdom), and reception of enrichment through Christ's poverty (2Cor 8:9 — "you might become rich").

Inner closure is specifically the impairment of the capacity to receive from God: "I need nothing" (Rev 3:17) is the self-declaration that blocks reception. The counsel to "buy from me gold refined by fire" (Rev 3:18) is the divine invitation to receive — but the inner-closed person cannot receive because they do not believe they need anything.

Reverential fear can be received through instruction: Deu 31:12-13 (the assembled community receiving the formation of fear through hearing Torah — the community is positioned to receive); 2Ki 17:28 (a priest sent to teach the settlers "how to fear the Lord" — reception through instructed formation); Psa 34:11 (the psalmist's offer to "instruct children in fear of the Lord" — explicit receptive formation context).

The "do not fear" command is received by the person who is gripped by acute fear: Lam 3:57 (divine response to the inner cry: "God drew near and spoke 'Do not fear' — the divine response to the inner cry is direct personal reassurance, addressing fear with the intimacy of God's nearness"). The reception requires the will's openness to the divine word.

Terror-as-weapon is "received" involuntarily by enemy peoples: Gen 35:5 (terror falling on surrounding cities — no choice in reception); Exo 23:27 (God's terror working on enemy peoples' inner being — involuntary imposition).

The receiving direction shows three modes: (1) voluntary formed reception — reverential fear received through instruction (M01-A); (2) commanded-release reception — the frightened person receiving the command that releases acute fear (M01-B-VCG-06); (3) involuntary imposition — terror received against the will of the recipients (M01-C-VCG-01).

Yes. The recipient-experience corpus (M02-B-VCG-07) evidences receiving wrath from God: Job 6:4 (poison his spirit drinks); Psa 88:16 (sweeping destroying force assaulting from within); Mic 7:9 (willingly bearing God's rage as consequence). The provocation corpus (M02-D-VCG-02) evidences receiving provocation from another human: Hannah receiving Peninnah's sustained provocation (1Sa 1:6–7); Eph 6:4 (children receiving provocation from fathers).

Grief is received from another when the other's actions, words, or state become the occasion for grief in the person. David's grief over Absalom's death is received from the news of his son's death through Joab's report (2Sa 19:1 — M03-A-VCG-01). The elders receive grief from Paul's announcement that they will not see his face again (Act 20:38 — M03-D-VCG-05 anchor). The Corinthians receive grief through Paul's letter (2Cor 7:8 — M03-C-VCG-02). The tu.gah grief of a mother from her foolish son (Pro 10:1 — M03-C-VCG-01) is grief inflicted upon one person through another's failure.

**[CHAR-1]** E — In the divine-to-human direction: the people receive God's exultation over them (Zep 3:17; Jer 32:41), and the effect of knowing God exults over them appears to generate responsive exultation in them. Deu 30:9's promise that God will "again take delight in prospering you" implies the people's experience of being the object of divine delight. In the human-to-human direction: Pro 23:24–25 implies the righteous son's awareness of his parents' joy; Isa 66:10 implies Jerusalem receiving the solidarity-exultation of those who love her.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. (1) **Received from news** — Luk 1:14 (Zechariah will have joy; many will rejoice at John's birth); Act 15:3 (great joy brought to the brothers); Act 15:31 (rejoicing at the encouraging letter); (2) **Received from community** — Phile 20 ("refresh my heart in Christ") — Paul receiving joy from Philemon's response; 2Cor 7:13 (Paul's joy increased by hearing of Titus's refreshment); 1Th 3:9 (Paul's overflowing joy at the Thessalonians' faithfulness); (3) **Received from a person's return** — Act 12:14 (Rhoda's joy at Peter's voice); Phili 2:28 (Philippians' joy at seeing Epaphroditus); 2Ti 1:4 (Paul longing to be filled with joy at seeing Timothy).

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes: Act 16:34 (the jailer's household receives the characteristic from the jailer's faith-joy — they all rejoice together); Luk 1:44 (Elizabeth's baby leaps for joy at receiving the Spirit-gladness transmitted through Mary's greeting — the most physicality-affirming reception in the corpus); the communities addressed in Mat 5:12 and 1Pe 4:13 receive the characteristic through apostolic command that channels the Spirit's work. Joh 8:56 (Abraham's agalliao at Christ's day coming) — reception through prophetic-faith perception of a future reality.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. (1) **Received through good news** — Pro 12:25 (the weighed-down heart receives gladness from a good word); Pro 15:30 (bones refreshed by good news received); Isa 39:8 (Hezekiah receiving Isaiah's word as good); Gen 40:16 (baker receiving Joseph's interpretation as favorable); 2Sa 18:27 (David's expectant reception of the runner's good news); (2) **Received through testimony** — Neh 2:18 (the people's inner resolve stirred by receiving Nehemiah's testimony of God's good hand); (3) **Received as inner wellbeing through God's acts** — 1Sa 16:23 (Saul receiving inner refreshment through David's music); 1Sa 11:9 (men of Jabesh receiving the good news of deliverance); (4) **Received as declared blessedness** — makarismos (Rom 4:6, 9 — blessedness declared over Abraham and received by faith).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes: (1) **Received divine Delight** — the dominant instance: Psa 18:19 (rescue received because God delighted in David); 1Ki 10:9 (throne received because God delighted in Solomon); Isa 62:4 (new name and covenantal restoration received from God's Delight); (2) **Received human relational Delight** — 1Sa 18:22 (David told the king delights in you — whether genuine or false); 1Sa 19:1 (Jonathan's Delight received by David as protection); 1Th 2:8 (the Thessalonians receiving Paul's self-giving from his relational Delight); (3) **Received consolation-Delight** — Psa 94:19 (soul cheered by God's consolations — sha.a received into the overwhelmed inner being); (4) **Received parental Delight** — Mic 1:16's children as "children of your delight" implicitly receive the parent's tender attachment; (5) **Received obedience-pleasing** — 1Jo 3:22 (prayers answered as the received consequence of pleasing God through obedience).

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes: (1) **Received relational pleasantness** — 2Sa 1:26 (David receiving Jonathan's pleasantness; the quality of Jonathan's companionship was a Pleasure received by David's inner being); Song 1:16; 7:6 (the lover receiving the beloved's pleasantness); (2) **Received speech-Pleasure** — Pro 16:24 (gracious words received by the soul — an inner being receiving pleasant speech from another); Pro 2:10's "pleasant to your soul" implies a received quality; (3) **Received material pleasantness** — 2Sa 1:24 (daughters of Israel receiving the luxury of Saul's scarlet and gold); Jer 51:34 (Jerusalem's delicacies received — and then consumed by the enemy); (4) **Received communal Pleasure** — Psa 133:1 (each brother receiving the pleasantness of the unified community).

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes: (1) **Received from the worshipping community** — the entire VCG-01 Tell-Remember tradition is a received-tradition: "we will tell to the coming generation" (Psa 78:4) — the coming generation receives Wonder through being told; "he has caused his wondrous works to be remembered" (Psa 111:4) — God ensures the Wonder is receivable; (2) **Received from God directly** — Psa 119:18's "open my eyes, that I may behold" — Wonder received as a God-given perceptive capacity; (3) **2Sa 1:26** — David receiving Jonathan's extraordinary love; (4) **Mar 1:27** — the crowd receiving the wonder-shock of Jesus' authoritative exorcism; **Mar 10:24** — disciples receiving amazement from Jesus' teaching.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Reception is evidenced for all seven. The most analytically significant comparative finding: the receiving direction reveals different primary mediums for each characteristic: (1) **Joy (Char 2)**: received primarily through news, report, and visible returning persons (Act 12:14; Phili 2:28; Act 15:3); (2) **Gladness (Char 3)**: received primarily through spoken words — the apt word, good news, testimony (Pro 12:25; Neh 2:18); (3) **Delight (Char 4)**: received primarily from divine action — rescue, exaltation, naming (Psa 18:19; Isa 62:4); (4) **Pleasure (Char 5)**: received from persons, their pleasantness, and their speech (2Sa 1:26; Pro 16:24); (5) **Wonder (Char 6)**: received from the community's witness-tradition and from direct encounter with God's wondrous acts (Psa 78:4; Psa 107:24); (6) **Suffering-Joy (Char 7)**: received within community through shared faith-crisis (Act 16:34's household) and Spirit-transmission (Luk 1:44's in-utero response); (7) **Exultation (Char 1)**: received from God's exultation over the person (Zep 3:17) as the primary instance — human-to-human receiving is less documented. The mediums confirm the characteristics' different relational modes: Joy through news; Gladness through speech; Pleasure through persons; Wonder through tradition and encounter; Suffering-Joy through Spirit-in-community.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, extensively in M07-A. The unjust-wound register (M07-A-VCG-01, -02) is almost entirely about shame received — the psalmist whose honour is exchanged for shame by enemies' deceit (Psa 4:2), Israel whose shame comes from surrounding nations (Eze 34:29; 36:6; 36:15), the mother whose shame comes from bereavement (Jer 15:9), the servants who receive shame through drought and helplessness (Jer 14:3-4). Received shame is the primary operational mode in the unjust-wound register. The corrective-shame register (M07-B-VCG-05; M07-C-VCG-03) also operates as received — the community receiving Paul's shame-direction (1Cor 6:5), Israel receiving the shame of the temple's design (Eze 43:10).

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 is primarily a received characteristic. What enables receiving CHAR-2 to be transformative (corrective) rather than merely destructive is the person's willingness to recognise their proper standing. The envoys accept the king's compassion and wait for restoration (2Sa 10:5). What blocks transformation is the hardened pride that cannot integrate the corrective signal.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — Paul receives dishonour (2Cor 6:8, vc=34963) without altering inner integrity — the key condition for receiving structural dishonour without inner displacement is the grounded knowledge of one's own standing before God. The poor man receives dishonour (Jam 2:6) — the evidence does not describe his inner response but implies that his worth before God is real regardless of the community's misassignment.

---

**[CHAR-4]** S — The corpus does not extensively describe a person receiving CHAR-4 from another — CHAR-4 is primarily produced within the individual conscience through its own evaluative operation. Silent on extensive evidence for the receiving direction.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 is primarily a received characteristic. What enables the person to receive CHAR-5 without being defined by it is grounded confidence in God's worth-assignment. The Galatians' non-contemptuous reception of Paul (Gal 4:14) — "received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus" — shows the alternative to CHAR-5's worth-cancellation: seeing through the physical weakness to the divine messenger behind it. The one who cannot receive CHAR-5 without being damaged is the one whose self-worth is entirely dependent on others' contempt-or-approval judgments.

---

**[CHAR-6]** S — CHAR-6 is not typically received from another person — it is maintained within the person through their own moral choices. The only receiving context is the divine confirmation (God confirming Abimelech's innocence, Gen 20:6) — but this is God validating CHAR-6 rather than God extending CHAR-6 to the person. Silent on receiving direction as an interpersonal dynamic.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The human receiving of M07's characteristics is the dominant mode across the cluster — five of six characteristics are primarily received conditions. What distinguishes redemptive from destructive reception is consistent across all five: the person's inner orientation when the characteristic arrives. The trusting person receives shame without being defined by it (Char 1); the person open to correction receives the corrective signal (Char 2); the grounded person receives dishonour without inner displacement (Char 3 — Paul's "through honor and dishonor" in 2Cor 6:8); the conscientious person receives the moral evaluation and renounces (Char 4); the called person receives contempt and blesses in return (Char 5 — 1Pe 3:9). In each case the orientation toward God — trust, openness to correction, grounded confidence, active moral engagement, willingness to bless — is the inner condition that transforms receiving from destructive to redemptive.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes — as the crushing experience of contempt, oppressive dominance, and sustained trampling. Psa 123:4 (vc=33953, M08-A4-VCG-03): "our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those who are at ease, of the contempt of the proud" — reception of CHAR-1 as saturating contempt that overwhelms the inner person. Psa 13:2 (vc=34241, M08-A4-VCG-03): the enemy's exaltation over the psalmist produces "sorrow in my heart all the day" — reception as sustained oppressive weight on the inner person. Psa 56:2 (vc=34163, M08-A4-VCG-03): "my enemies trample on me all day long, for many attack me proudly" — reception as sustained physical and relational assault operating "from a position of felt superiority." Psa 140:5 (vc=33954, M08-A4-VCG-02): "the arrogant have hidden a trap for me, and with cords they have spread a net" — reception as calculating predatory entrapment.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes — as sustained oppression and unjust social aggression. Psa 119:51 (vc=34099, M08-B-VCG-02): "the insolent utterly deride me, yet I do not turn away from your law" — the psalmist receives sustained contemptuous derision from the insolent. Psa 119:85 (vc=34102): "the insolent have dug pitfalls for me" — predatory entrapment as the form of received CHAR-2. Psa 119:122 (vc=34103): "let not the insolent oppress me" — oppression as the sustained experience of receiving CHAR-2 from another. Psa 86:14 (vc=34097): "a band of ruthless men seek my life; they do not set God before them."

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. 2Cor 9:4 (vc=33920, M08-C-VCG-03): Paul and the Macedonians arriving to find the Corinthians unprepared would receive Paul's boasting about their readiness as an exposed empty claim — the boasting creates a social debt in those who receive it. 1Cor 5:6 (vc=33903, M08-C-VCG-01): the community receiving its members' boasting undergoes corruption (leaven) — the boast is received by the community and produces internal moral decay. VCG-03: 2Cor 1:14 (vc=33907): mutual boasting — each receiving the other's boasting as relational affirmation.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — as communal disorder and relational disruption. 2Cor 12:20 (vc=33942, M08-D-VCG-02): fusiōsis in a cluster of relational sins that Paul fears finding in Corinth — the community receives CHAR-4 as one element of a broader relational disorder pattern. 1Cor 5:2 (vc=33940, M08-D-VCG-01): the community that should be mourning is instead puffed up — the community as a whole has received CHAR-4's cognitive distortion, preventing collective appropriate response to moral failure.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes — as structural exploitation and social neglect. Eze 16:49 (vc=33979, M08-E-VCG-01): the poor and needy receive CHAR-5 as the absence of aid from those with structural power and ease — received as social abandonment. Hab 2:9 (vc=34169, M08-E-VCG-02): those from whom unjust gain is taken receive CHAR-5 as economic exploitation in the service of another's self-securing elevation. The victims of CHAR-5 are primarily those with less structural power — the poor (Eze 16:49), those exploited for another's gain (Hab 2:9).

**[CLUSTER]** E — All five characteristics are received by others. The cluster comparison reveals that the primary recipients of M08 are the vulnerable and the godly: the poor (CHAR-5 — Eze 16:49, M08-E-VCG-01), the psalmist (CHAR-1 — Psa 123:4, M08-A4-VCG-03; CHAR-2 — Psa 119:51/85, M08-B-VCG-02), the community (CHAR-3 VCG-01 — 1Cor 5:6, M08-C-VCG-01), the apostolic community (CHAR-4 — the Corinthian puffed-up community). The cluster-synthesis: M08's primary victims are the humble and the weak — those who lack the structural power, social standing, or cognitive authority to resist the characteristic directed toward them. Pride consistently targets the vulnerable.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, in the community and apostolic registers. 2Cor7:15 — Titus receives the Corinthians' obedient welcome with fear and trembling; his affection deepens in response. Phile21 — Paul writes with confidence that Philemon's obedience will be received (he will receive the expression of Philemon's submission). 1Ti3:4 — the overseer whose children are submissive receives their submission as a sign of his household order and character. The person in authority receives the submission as both a relational expression and a vindication of the authority structure.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The two-verse corpus does not evidence contrition being received horizontally from another person. The characteristic is a state the person is in before God; its reception in the sense of one person receiving contrition from another is not evidenced.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heb5:2 evidences reception: the "ignorant and wayward" receive the high priest's metriopatheō — they are the recipients of his measured gentle dealing. The erring persons receive a form of engagement that is calibrated and compassionate rather than severe. The receiving of this characteristic is the experience of being dealt with gently rather than harshly when one has erred.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. 1Ti3:4 — the overseer's children receive the effects of his semnotēs in the form of orderly, respectful compliance — they receive the character-quality's relational ordering. Tit2:7 — the hearers receive teaching that is authenticated by the teacher's semnotēs — they receive instruction whose credibility is established by the teacher's dignity. The reception is not the characteristic itself but its effects: orderly response and authentic teaching-reception.

**[CHAR-6]** E — 1Ch28:21 — Solomon and the temple-building project receive the willing-hearted service of the craftsmen — their service is received as a gift of willing engagement rather than compelled labour. God receives the willing-hearted offerings (Exo35:5/22; 2Ch29:31) — the willing-hearted person extends free offering; God receives it. The receiving direction is most clearly evidenced in God's reception of the free offerings and in Solomon's reception of the willing skilled service.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The receiving direction is less directly evidenced than the giving direction, but it is present. In Luk1:48, Mary receives the divine acknowledgement of her humble estate — God looks upon her humility and she receives his favour as a consequence. In the horizontal direction, the community that encounters Paul's humility (Act20:19; 2Cor11:7) receives the benefit of his self-lowering — the Corinthians' exaltation (2Cor11:7) is the received effect of Paul's self-humbling. In Eph4:2 and Phili2:3, the posture of humility toward one another creates a relational environment that the other person receives as genuine regard. The receiving of humility from another is evidenced as the reception of the other's genuine regard and self-lowering on one's behalf.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The receiving direction is evidenced across the cluster, but with different recipient profiles. CHAR-1: others receive the humble person's genuine regard; Mary receives divine acknowledgment of her humble estate (Luk1:48). CHAR-2: the authority receives submission from the one yielding; 2Cor7:15 — Titus receives the Corinthians' obedient welcome. CHAR-3: not directly evidenced in horizontal receiving — the characteristic is not received from another person; it is a state the person is in before God. CHAR-4: the erring receive the high priest's metriopatheō (Heb5:2). CHAR-5: the overseer's children receive orderly compliance-evoked-by-dignity (1Ti3:4); the hearers receive teaching authenticated by the teacher's semnotēs. CHAR-6: God receives the freely-offered worship; Solomon receives the willing service of craftsmen. Cluster-level: the pattern of who receives what from whom varies by characteristic's relational structure — CHAR-1 and CHAR-5 produce ordered responses in others; CHAR-2, CHAR-4, and CHAR-6 produce structured giving and receiving relationships. CHAR-3 remains the cluster's exclusively-before-God characteristic throughout the relational interface analysis.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The recipient of sinning is extensively evidenced in VCG-02. Gen 20:9 — Abimelech receives sinning from Abraham: "you have brought on me and my kingdom a great sin." Gen 42:22 — Joseph received sinning from his brothers: "Do not sin against the boy." 1Sa 19:4/5 — David as the would-be recipient of Saul's sinning: "Let not the king sin against his servant David." Mat 18:15 — the brother who has been sinned against and must decide whether to confront. 1Cor 8:12 — the weak brother whose conscience is wounded by another's sinning. The reception operates as a *harm received* — moral, relational, and sometimes physical damage inflicted on the recipient by the sinner's act.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Yes. (1) *Enticement received*: 2Pe 2:18 — "those who are barely escaping from those who live in error" receive the enticement directed at them by the false teachers; the mechanism is received by those at the vulnerable threshold between error and escape. (2) *Hypocrisy received*: Gal 2:13 — "even Barnabas was led astray by their hypocrisy" — Barnabas receives the collective hypocrisy and is drawn into it; the reception is described as "being led astray" — passive in form, showing the mechanism's power over the receiver.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Yes — the reception dimension is the condition's defining feature. (1) *Universal reception through Adam*: Rom 5:12 — "death spread to all men because all sinned" — the universal condition is received by all humanity through the Adamic representative structure; Joh 9:34 — "born in utter sin" — the condition is received at birth; (2) *Reception of forgiveness as the reversal*: VCG-02 throughout — "your sins are forgiven" (Mat 9:2) — the forgiveness is received by the person from Jesus; (3) *Reception of the Spirit's conviction*: Joh 16:8 — the Spirit convicts the world — the condition's recognition is received from the Spirit's external work.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Yes — the reception is the enslaving mechanism's primary operation. Joh 8:34 — "everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin" — the slavery is received through the practice: the person receives the enslaved state as the constitutional consequence of sustained sinning practice. Gal 3:22 — "imprisoned everything under sin" — the universal imprisonment is the structural condition received by all persons under the declaration of Scripture; the reception is universal and not individually chosen but corporately received.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Yes — through multiple reception modes. Luk 17:3-4 — the one who sins and repents ("I repent") is to receive forgiveness from the offended party. The reception in this context is the relational resolution — the claim is released by the other, and the offender receives the release. **How reception operates:** The clearest account is Luk 7:47 — the woman who has received forgiveness demonstrates its reception through bodily acts (weeping, anointing) and through the love-orientation produced. The reception is inner and transformative — it generates a new orientation rather than merely relieving a pressure.

The data addresses reception of compassion from God toward the human person extensively (covered at T4.1), but reception of compassion from one human person to another is partially evidenced and the inner-being dynamics of reception are largely unaddressed.

**What is evidenced:** Gen 19:16 — Lot receives divine compassion (chem.lah) when the angels physically take him and his family by the hand and lead them out. The reception is enacted bodily — the compassion-act reaches him physically and produces rescue. Isa 57:18 — the straying person receives divine comfort (ni.chum) — "I will heal him; I will lead him and restore comfort to him." The reception produces healing and restoration.

In the Synoptic pattern, the recipients of Jesus's splanchnizō-movements receive healing (Matt 20:34 — "their eyes were opened"), restoration (Luke 7:14-15 — the widow's son raised), and feeding (Matt 15:32ff). The reception of compassion in these contexts produces material change in the recipient's condition.

**What is missing (P):** The inner-being dynamics of receiving compassion — what happens inside the person at the moment of reception — are almost entirely absent from the data. The focus of the vocabulary is on the giver's inner movement and the outer act of compassion, not on the receiver's inner experience. The gap identified at T1.5 P1 (receiver's immediate inner response) is reproduced and deepened here.
